2609.07344.title: Staying on the Attack Path: Structured State for Long-Horizon Automated Penetration Testing
2609.07344.paper_summary: Large language model (LLM) based agents are increasingly applied to cybersecurity tasks such as vulnerability discovery and automated penetration testing. On long-horizon security tasks, however, such agents remain limited by context forgetting and intent drift: early critical facts and causal reasoning chains are lost over extended interactions, and the agent falls into aimless, repetitive exploration. This paper proposes Intentest, an intent-graph-guided automated penetration testing agent that externalizes long-horizon state from the LLM's context window onto a persistent fact-intent directed acyclic graph (DAG), thereby substantially reducing invalid transitions. We evaluate Intentest on automated penetration testing of web applications, a representative long-tail task in cybersecurity. In the DAG, verified network states are stored as immutable fact nodes, and exploration directions are constrained as intent edges bounded by predecessor facts. The system adopts a three-layer architecture, in which the fact-intent mapping layer maintains the global state, the task scheduling and allocation layer ensures execution stability through two-phase degradation recovery and multi-dimensional adaptive load balancing, and the intent retrieval and prediction layer provides tactical priors through a top-down five-stage filtering algorithm. On a benchmark of real CTF challenges covering more than ten vulnerability types across three difficulty levels, Intentest achieves an overall success rate of 88.2% and a success rate of 75.0% on hard tasks, improving over the baseline by approximately 44 and 50 percentage points. Ablation experiments further show that the intent retrieval and prediction reduce the average number of rounds on successful medium and hard tasks by about 33% and 48%, respectively, without changing the set of solvable tasks.
2609.07344.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型（LLM）基礎的代理越來越多地應用於網絡安全任務，例如漏洞發現和自動滲透測試。<lb/>然而，在長期的安全任務中，這些代理仍然受到上下文遺忘和意圖漂移的限制：早期的關鍵事實和因果推理鏈在長時間的互動中丟失，代理陷入無目的的重複探索。<lb/>本文提出了Intentest，一種意圖圖引導的自動滲透測試代理，將長期狀態從LLM的上下文窗口外部化到一個持久的事實-意圖有向無環圖（DAG）中，從而大幅減少無效轉換。<lb/>我們在自動滲透測試網絡應用程序的實驗中評估了Intentest，這是一個在網絡安全中具有代表性的長尾任務。<lb/>在DAG中，經過驗證的網絡狀態作為不可變的事實節點存儲，探索方向作為受前驅事實約束的意圖邊緣進行限制。<lb/>該系統採用三層架構，其中事實-意圖映射層維護全局狀態，任務調度和分配層通過兩階段降級恢復和多維自適應負載平衡確保執行穩定性，意圖檢索和預測層通過自上而下的五階段過濾算法提供戰術先驗。<lb/>在涵蓋三個難度級別的十多種漏洞類型的真實CTF挑戰基準中，Intentest的整體成功率達到88.2%，在困難任務中的成功率為75.0%，相較基準提高了約44和50個百分點。<lb/>消融實驗進一步顯示，意圖檢索和預測在成功的中等和困難任務中分別減少了平均回合數約33%和48%，而不改變可解決任務的集合。
